whyCheapBearCase.answer: PTC trades at a moderate P/E (14.68) for a software company with strong historical margins, and the stock is down modestly over six months (-5.87%) despite a positive three-month return (+8.0%) [source: 1] - a divergence a cached headline captures directly: 'Has PTC (PTC) Fallen Enough To Look Reasonable?' (Yahoo, 2026-08-09) [source: 7]. The filing evidence gives a real, quantified reason for caution: GAAP revenue actually declined 7% year-over-year in fiscal Q3 2026 ($600.0 million vs $643.9 million in Q3 2025, 8% on a constant-currency basis), which the 10-Q attributes to the Q2 2026 divestiture of the Kepware and ThingWorx businesses (which contributed $46 million of revenue in Q3 2025) plus 'lower license revenue due primarily to the shortened duration of a single large contract renewal and expansion' [source: 2]. GAAP operating margin fell approximately 480 basis points year-over-year in the same quarter, and GAAP diluted EPS fell 12% to $1.03 from $1.17 [source: 2]. Headline ARR (annual recurring revenue) was essentially flat year-over-year at $2.41 billion (0% actual, +2% constant currency) [source: 2] - a real deceleration versus PTC's FY2025 ARR growth of 10% (8% constant currency) reported in the 10-K [source: 3], even though ARR excluding the divested businesses grew a healthier 7% (9% constant currency) [source: 2].

revenueEpsTrend.answer: Mixed: reported GAAP revenue is contracting in the most recent quarter due to a divestiture and a license-timing effect, while underlying recurring revenue and non-GAAP earnings continue to grow. Q3 FY2026 GAAP revenue was $600.0 million versus $643.9 million in Q3 FY2025, down 7% (8% constant currency), driven by the Kepware/ThingWorx divestiture and a shortened large contract renewal [source: 2]. However, ARR excluding the divested businesses grew 7% (9% constant currency) year-over-year [source: 2], and nine-month FY2026 GAAP net income was $876.0 million versus $386.2 million in the nine months of FY2025 (+126.8%), though this is substantially inflated by a one-time $462.6 million non-operating gain recognized in Q2 FY2026 on the sale of the Kepware and ThingWorx businesses [source: 2]. Excluding that one-time item, nine-month non-GAAP diluted EPS grew from $4.53 to $6.21 (+37.1%), and nine-month non-GAAP net income grew from $547.5 million to $731.5 million (+33.6%) [source: 2]. For the full prior fiscal year, the 10-K shows FY2025 total revenue of $2,739.2 million versus $2,298.5 million in FY2024 (+19%, +18% constant currency), with GAAP diluted EPS of $6.08 versus $3.12 (+95%) [source: 3]. So the multi-period picture is one of strong FY2025 growth, followed by a genuine Q3 FY2026 GAAP revenue contraction concentrated around the divestiture and a large-contract renewal timing effect, with underlying (ex-divested) ARR and non-GAAP profitability both still growing.

marginTrend.answer: Compressing in the most recent quarter, after a period of strong expansion. GAAP operating margin in Q3 FY2026 was approximately 27.8% ($166.5M / $600.0M) versus approximately 32.6% in Q3 FY2025 ($209.8M / $643.9M), a decline of roughly 480 basis points, which the 10-Q attributes directly to lower revenue in the quarter [source: 2]. This follows dramatic full-year margin expansion in FY2025: the 10-K's own results table shows GAAP operating margin rose to 36% in FY2025 from 26% in FY2024 (non-GAAP operating margin 48% vs 39%), with GAAP operating income up 67% to $982.4 million from $588.1 million [source: 3]. Nine-month FY2026 GAAP operating income of $683.4 million is still up 24.5% versus $548.8 million in the nine months of FY2025 [source: 2], so the margin compression identified above is a Q3-specific, revenue-driven effect rather than a reversal of the broader FY2025 margin-expansion trend.

guidanceChange.answer: Not determinable from available sources. No explicit forward revenue, ARR, margin, or EPS guidance range for the remainder of FY2026 or FY2027 was found in the extracted MD&A or Risk Factors text of either filing. A cached headline, 'PTC (PTC) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript' (Yahoo, 2026-08-08) [source: 8], would likely contain forward guidance commentary from the earnings call, but only the headline was cached for this pipeline, not the transcript content, so no guidance direction can be stated from it.

catalysts.text: Portfolio streamlining via the Kepware and ThingWorx divestiture in Q2 FY2026, which generated a $462.6 million gain and $500 million of the quarter's $525 million share repurchase, while underlying ARR excluding those divested businesses continued to grow 7% (9% constant currency) year-over-year.

AI product investment: a cached headline confirms 'PTC (PTC) Rolls Out AI Tools Across ALM And PLM Workflows' (Yahoo, 2026-08-08), indicating active product expansion into AI-enabled application lifecycle and product lifecycle management tooling, though the article content itself was not fetched.

Continued strong free cash flow growth: nine-month FY2026 free cash flow of $835.0 million versus $756.2 million in the nine months of FY2025 (+10.4%), and cash from operations up 11.5% to $851.3 million, funding both the divestiture-linked buyback and ongoing capital return.

risks.text: Real, filing-confirmed GAAP revenue contraction in the most recent quarter (-7% YoY), driven partly by a structural change (the Kepware/ThingWorx divestiture) but also by 'the shortened duration of a single large contract renewal and expansion' - a customer-concentration-flavored timing risk that could recur.

Q3 FY2026 operating margin compression of approximately 480 basis points year-over-year, directly attributed by management to the lower revenue base - a real, quantified near-term profitability headwind, not merely a comparison-period artifact.

The large year-over-year net income and EPS growth figures for the nine-month period are substantially inflated by a one-time $462.6 million divestiture gain; investors relying on GAAP net income or EPS growth rates without adjusting for this one-time item would materially overstate the company's organic earnings growth.

Increased near-term leverage to fund buybacks: $225 million of net debt borrowings under the company's credit facility in Q3 FY2026 alone, partially funding a $525 million share repurchase - a real, if modest (debt/equity 0.15), increase in balance-sheet risk.

verdict.reasoning: The filing evidence shows a real, quantified GAAP revenue contraction and margin compression in the most recent quarter, tied to a specific divestiture and a large-contract renewal timing effect [source: 2] - not simply headline noise. At the same time, ARR excluding the divested businesses continued to grow at a healthy 7-9% clip, free cash flow grew double digits, and FY2025 (the most recent full fiscal year) showed strong revenue and margin expansion [source: 2, 3], all suggesting the underlying subscription business remains healthy. The moderate P/E (14.68) [source: 1] does not scream 'statistically cheap value opportunity' the way some other tickers in this batch do, and the very large nine-month GAAP net income growth figure is substantially a one-time divestiture-gain artifact that should not be mistaken for organic earnings momentum [source: 2]. Confidence is medium because no forward guidance was available in the extracted filing text to confirm whether the Q3 revenue/margin pressure is expected to persist or reverse, and because this is a newly-researched ticker with no prior research pass to cross-check against.
